description: Composite TEM figure of a Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si austenitic low-density steel after tensile deformation at two temperatures. (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph (scale bar 1 µm) of the sample deformed at -196 °C: dark parallel band-like features in a heavily dislocated matrix are annotated "Mechanical twins" with red arrows, a white circle marks one band, and "Dislocations" is labelled with a white arrow. A bottom-right SAED inset of (a) has a 10 1/nm scale bar, is recorded along zone axis Z.A. [1,1,0], and shows strong spots indexed (1,-1,1), (0,0,2), (0,0,-2), (1,-1,-1) with additional spotted rows consistent with twin-related reflections. (b) is a bright-field TEM micrograph (scale bar 2 µm) of the sample deformed at -77 °C; orange dashed lines trace two intersecting straight bands labelled "Traces of {111} slip planes", with "Dislocations" pointed out by a white arrow on a banded, dislocation-dense matrix. Together the panels show that cryogenic (-196 °C, low SFE) deformation produces mechanical twinning plus dense dislocation activity, whereas at -77 °C deformation proceeds by planar glide giving microbands along {111} planes; no numeric values are printed on either panel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph (scale bar 1 µm) of the sample tensile deformed at -196 °C. Dark elongated band-like features are annotated 'Mechanical twins' with red arrows; one band is circled in white. A white arrow labels 'Dislocations' in the heavily dislocated matrix. Bottom-right inset is an SAED pattern (scale bar 10 1/nm) along Z.A. [1,1,0] with reflections labelled (1,-1,1), (0,0,2), (0,0,-2) and (1,-1,-1).

Bright-field TEM micrograph (scale bar 2 µm) of the sample tensile deformed at -77 °C. Orange dashed lines mark two intersecting straight straight bands labelled 'Traces of {111} slip planes'; a white arrow labels 'Dislocations'. Matrix is dark and dislocation-dense. No SAED inset is visible in this panel at the supplied resolution.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph whose dark parallel banded features are annotated 'Mechanical twins' with red arrows, with one band marked by a white circle.
Panel (a) contains a lower-right SAED inset with a 10 1/nm scale bar recorded along zone axis Z.A. [1,1,0], with legible reflection labels (1,-1,1), (0,0,2), (0,0,-2) and (1,-1,-1).
Panel (a) carries a 1 µm scale bar and panel (b) carries a 2 µm scale bar.
Panel (b) shows two intersecting straight bands marked by orange dashed lines and labelled 'Traces of {111} slip planes', with 'Dislocations' indicated by a white arrow.
No SAED inset is visible in panel (b) in the supplied image, although the citing text refers to a corresponding SAED pattern for the -77 °C sample.
The caption states (a) is a TEM image of the sample tensile deformed at -196 °C together with its corresponding SAED pattern.
The caption states (b) shows microbands of the sample tensile deformed at -77 °C.
The citing text states that the mechanical twinning plane formed along <112> crystal direction on {111} plane in the case of the grain oriented near <110> zone axis.
The citing text states that, compared with the sample deformed at -196 °C, no mechanical twins but microbands are observed in the sample deformed at -77 °C.

The citing text states that the corresponding SAED pattern indicates these bands are orientated along {111} planes, and that planar glide gives a uniform and dense distribution of microbands, characteristic of austenitic low density steels [27,28].

The citing text uses this figure to argue that products of planar glide such as mechanical twins and glide bands act as barriers to partial-dislocation motion, contributing to a high work hardening rate.

unreadable_items: panel (a) SAED inset: only part of the reflection labels are legible (e.g. (1,-1,1), (0,0,2), (0,0,-2), (1,-1,-1)); additional spot indices and any twin/double-diffraction annotation are unreadable
panel (b): no SAED pattern is present in the supplied image, so the {111} band orientation claimed in the citing text cannot be verified from pixels
